Oliver Hannaoui

Greetings! I am a second-year Statistics PhD student at Carnegie Mellon University. I am also a member of Delphi, where I am working on leveraging time-series foundation models for infectious disease forecasting.
Previously, I completed an M1 in Applied Mathematics and Statistics at the Polytechnic Institute of Paris. Prior to that, I spent two formative years at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York as a Senior Research Analyst in the Financial Intermediation group. 
I can be contacted via e-mail or LinkedIn .



Photo taken from the bleacher seats inside the best stadium in the MLB.

Coffee Rankings
I spend more time (and money) at coffee shops than I would like to admit. Below is a running ranking of my favorite coffee shops in several locations I have spent a non-trivial amount of time living in.



Pittsburgh










#
Name
Notes




1
KLVN Coffee Lab
I found this place by accident on Google Maps and have had a hard time making an excuse to frequent other coffee shops since.


2
Mechanic Coffee
I would say they have the best coffee in Pittsburgh.


3
Creative Chem Co
Newer establishment with an incredibly creative interior design and friendly staff.


4
Shibam Coffee
Best hours of all coffee shops in Pittsburgh (7am - 11pm everyday).


5
Commonplace Coffee
Favorite place to go to buy coffee beans for drip coffee.








Paris










#
Name
Notes




1
Terres de Cafe
A chain with several locations, still the highest quality coffee I've had.


2
Noir
Even with 18 locations the quality is consistently great. I wish the seating was as functional as it is aesthetic though.


3
Dose
Really nice spot to go hang out at for Sunday brunch.


4
Araku
Most of my visits were on coffee breaks from the adjacent BSG library. Great coffee.


5
Aura
Feels like you're working out of a café in Newport Beach. Really good drink and food options.





I have to say that I spent too much time in the BSG library to get as much out of Parisian coffee shops as I would have liked. Going to coffee shops there on the weekends is also a bit of a gamble as many places don’t allow laptops.
Side note, I found this incredible website on all things Parisian coffee that I would have loved to have known about when I lived there.

Favorite place to work out of in East Village. I recommend the Honeynut Cheerio latte.

While very pricey, the quality is undeniable.

Cozy and underrated weekend spot.
